title: Count The Repetitions
statement:
Write `[s, n]` for the string made by placing `n` copies of `s` one after another, so `["ab", 3]` is `"ababab"`. A string `a` is said to be obtainable from a string `b` when deleting some (possibly none) of the characters of `b`, keeping the rest in order, leaves exactly `a`.

Let `str1 = [s1, n1]` and `str2 = [s2, n2]`. Return the largest integer `m` for which `[str2, m]` is obtainable from `str1`. If not even one copy of `str2` is obtainable, the answer is `0`.
constraints: s1 and s2 contain only lowercase English letters
signature: int getMaxRepetitions(String s1, int n1, String s2, int n2)
notes:
## Intuition

Since `[str2, m]` is just `s2` repeated `n2 · m` times, count how many copies of `s2` a greedy scan of `str1` can match and divide by `n2`. Scanning all of `str1` can take 10^8 steps (the brute force), but one copy of `s1` behaves the same whenever it starts at the same position of `s2`. With only `s2.length` positions, some position repeats within `s2.length + 1` copies, and from then on the copies cycle. A hash map from position to the totals at that moment finds the cycle so it can be skipped with one multiplication.

## Approach

1. Keep `index` (position in `s2`), `count` (finished copies of `s2`) and `block` (copies of `s1` used).
2. Simulate one copy of `s1`: each matching character advances `index`; when it reaches `s2.length`, reset it to 0 and add one to `count`.
3. If `seen` already holds this `index`, the copies since then form a cycle of `cycleBlocks` copies that finish `cycleCount` copies of `s2`. Fit as many whole cycles as the remaining copies allow, add them to `block` and `count`, and clear `seen` so the jump happens once.
4. Record `index` with the current `block` and `count`, and continue until `block` reaches `n1`.
5. Return `Math.floor(count / n2)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s1 = "acb"`, `s2 = "ab"`. The first copy matches `a` and `b`, so `count = 1`, `index = 0`, `block = 1`, and `seen` stores `0 → [1, 1]`. The second copy does the same: `count = 2`, `block = 2`, and `index = 0` is already in `seen`. The cycle is 1 copy finishing 1 `s2`; `(4 - 2) / 1 = 2` cycles fit, so `block = 4` and `count = 4`. The loop stops and the answer is `floor(4 / 2) = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(|s1| · |s2|): at most |s2| + 1 copies of `s1` are simulated before the jump, and less than one cycle after it.
- Space: O(|s2|) for `seen`.

## Pitfalls

- Detect the cycle on the position in `s2` at copy boundaries, not on `count`; equal counts say nothing about the future.
- Only whole cycles may be skipped; the leftover copies after the jump must still be simulated.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `index` | position in `s2` of the next character to match |
| `count` | copies of `s2` matched so far |
| `block` | copies of `s1` consumed so far |
| `seen` | `index` at the end of a copy → `[block, count]` at that moment |
| `prevBlock`, `prevCount` | the recorded `block` and `count` when `index` was last seen |
| `cycleBlocks`, `cycleCount` | copies of `s1` in one cycle, and copies of `s2` it finishes |
| `cycles` | how many whole cycles still fit into the remaining copies |

narration.2: Remember, for each s2 position seen at the end of an s1 copy, how many copies had been used and finished.
narration.7: Process copies of s1 until all n1 of them are used.
narration.8: Walk through one copy of s1 character by character.
narration.9: Does this character match the next character s2 needs?
narration.10: Yes: move to the following character of s2.
narration.11: Did that complete a whole copy of s2?
narration.13: Count the finished copy; index was reset to start the next one.
narration.17: One more copy of s1 has been used.
narration.19: Was this s2 position already seen at the end of an earlier copy? Then the process repeats from here.
narration.21: How many copies of s1 one cycle takes...
narration.22: ...and how many copies of s2 it finishes.
narration.23: Count the whole cycles that still fit into the remaining copies of s1.
narration.24: Skip those copies in one step...
narration.25: ...and credit all the s2 copies they would have finished.
narration.26: Forget old positions so the jump is made only once.
narration.28: Record where this copy ended along with the totals so far.
narration.30: Every n2 copies of s2 form one copy of str2.
